definition: Agentic commerce (also referred to as agent-based commerce) describes an emerging form of e-commerce in which semi-autonomus and fully autonomous artificial intelligence (AI) agents independently execute purchasing and payment processes on behalf of users or organizations.
details: Unlike conventional digital commerce systems, which require direct human interaction at key decision points, agentic commerce systems are designed to search for products or services, evaluate options, make purchasing decisions, and complete payments without real-time human involvement. Existing within the broader fields of e-commerce, fintech, and artificial intelligence, agentic commerce combines generative AI, autonomous agents, application programming interfaces (APIs), and digital payment infrastructures to direct transactions with no direct human interaction.

explainer.lead: Agentic commerce is e-commerce run by AI agents that can shop and pay on their own, without you clicking "buy" each time. It could reshape how trillions of dollars in goods and services change hands.

tiers.eli5: Imagine you gave your very smart helper a list: "Get me a blue bike under $200, with good reviews, by Friday." The helper searches stores, compares bikes, picks one, and pays — all while you play video games. That's agentic commerce: software that shops for you instead of just showing you options.
tiers.practitioner: Agentic commerce systems combine LLMs, autonomous agents, merchant APIs, and payment rails to execute end-to-end transactions. Typical implementations use protocols like Google's UCP for product discovery, OpenAI/Stripe's ACP for cart and checkout, and AP2 for payment authorization. Key pitfalls include handling disputed transactions, ensuring agent authentication, and presenting product data in machine-readable formats for agent discoverability.
tiers.paperLevel: Agentic commerce is defined as e-commerce in which semi-autonomous and fully autonomous AI agents independently execute purchasing and payment processes on behalf of users or organizations, operating according to predefined preferences, rules, or constraints. The field lacks a single canonical formal model; rather, it is characterized by protocol-level specifications (UCP, ACP, AP2) that standardize agent-merchant interactions across discovery, cart management, checkout, and payment authorization. Known limits include slower U.S. adoption due to privacy restrictions, the need for structured merchant data formats, and unresolved legal questions around liability for unauthorized agent transactions.

explainer.example: A small business owner configures an agent to maintain office supplies: "Reorder A4 paper when stock falls below 10 reams, choose the supplier with 2-day delivery under $45 per case, use the corporate card." The agent monitors inventory via API, detects low stock, compares three suppliers, selects one meeting all criteria, places the order, and processes payment — all without the owner touching a keyboard.

usedIn.name: Qwen AI chatbot
usedIn.detail: Allows users to complete transactions directly within its interface, including food and drink orders via Taobao Instant Commerce and Alipay AI Pay.

usedIn.name: Alibaba Accio Work
usedIn.detail: An AI agent for small and medium-sized exporters that researches market demand, compares suppliers, and generates product listings.

usedIn.name: commercetools AgenticLift
usedIn.detail: Lets companies connect existing commerce systems to AI assistants like ChatGPT, Google Gemini, and Microsoft Copilot without replatforming.

usedIn.name: Alipay AI Pay
usedIn.detail: An AI payment processing service enabling businesses in China to receive payments via autonomous AI agents.

explainer.intuition: Instead of you browsing, comparing, and checking out, you delegate the entire shopping task to a software agent with a budget and rules.
howItWorks: A user configures an agent with preferences: price limits, quality criteria, delivery needs, and payment methods.
The agent searches across merchants and platforms, comparing options against the user's constraints.
It selects a product or service, creates a cart, and initiates checkout through standardized protocols.
Payment is executed autonomously via delegated credentials, with cryptographic mandates recording user authorization.
The agent monitors order status and fulfillment, with humans stepping in only for exceptions or periodic review.
explainer.whyItMatters: McKinsey projects $1 trillion in U.S. B2C retail revenue could flow through agentic commerce by 2030, with global opportunity at $3–5 trillion. It shifts commerce from human-initiated transactions to continuous automated micro-decisions, potentially restructuring supply chains, pricing, and brand relationships.
misconceptions: Agentic commerce is just AI chatbots recommending products — recommendation systems lack decision-making authority and cannot complete transactions autonomously.
It eliminates all human involvement — humans still set rules, handle exceptions, and supervise, though real-time interaction at each step is removed.
It is already mainstream everywhere — adoption is uneven, with Chinese tech firms moving faster than U.S. counterparts due to differing privacy and regulatory constraints.
